title: Educational Activity Strategy as a Subject of Psychological Research: A Theoretical Model
abstract: The relevance of the present study is determined by transformations of the educational environment, expansion of informal and digital learning formats, and the increasing role of learner agency, which necessitates moving beyond traditional approaches to the analysis of educational strategies. The absence of a comprehensive conceptualization of educational activity strategy as an integrative construct uniting goal-related, motivational, instrumental, and resource-based aspects of cognitive organization constitutes the core research problem. The aim of the article is to develop a theoretical model of educational activity strategy and to substantiate the possibilities of its operationalization in psychological research. The main methods employed include a theoretical review of contemporary studies on cognitive and metacognitive strategies, as well as theoretical modeling, which enabled the synthesis of empirical data into a unified conceptual framework. The resulting model of educational activity (EA) strategy delineates goal-oriented, motivational, instrumental, and resource components, manifested at both the cognitive and metacognitive level. The goal-oriented component involves setting goals and tasks at the cognitive level and reflection on goal setting at the metacognitive level. The motivational component reflects perceived value and interest in learning at the cognitive level, and reflexive evaluation of educational activity motives at the metacognitive level. The instrumental component comprises techniques for information processing at the cognitive level and a system supporting their implementation at the metacognitive level. The resource component pertains to assessing task accessibility relative to anticipated costs at the cognitive level and managing these resources by aligning personal readiness with the sufficiency of external resources at the metacognitive level. Within this model, educational activity strategy is defined as a set of methods by which an individual organizes their own cognition and development within the educational process, grounded in their agentive position and entailing conscious management of goals, resources, motives, and means during learning.
